quote: Case I : θ1 < θ2. Let X~GIW(α, θ1, λ, β) and Y~GIW(α, θ2, λ, β). Then gX(y)/gY(y) = [α^{θ1} θ1 (1 − α^{θ2}) [1 − (1 − α)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]^{θ2+1}] / [α^{θ2} θ2 (1 − α^{θ1}) [1 − (1 − α)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]^{θ1+1}]. Since θ1 < θ2, d/dx [gX(y)/gY(y)] < 0. Hence, gX(y)/gY(y) is decreasing in y. That is X ≤lr Y. The remaining statement follow from the implication (32).
family: GIW = inverse truncated negative binomial Weibull (generalized inverse Weibull), cdf G(y; α, θ, λ, β) = (α^θ/(1 − α^θ)) ([1 − (1 − α)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]^{−θ} − 1) with α, θ, λ, β parameters (α > 0, α ≠ 1; θ, λ, β > 0)

hypotheses.text: The four stochastic orders defined above are related to each other, have the following implications (see, Shaked and Shanthikumar (2007)): X ≤rhr Y ⇐ X ≤lr Y ⇒ X ≤hr Y ⇒ X ≤st Y.

conclusion.direction: X <=lr Y, i.e. GIW(α, θ1, λ, β) <=lr GIW(α, θ2, λ, β) for θ1 < θ2 (hence <=hr, <=st, >=rhr direction reversed: X <=rhr Y follows per printed implication)

quote: Case II : α2 < α1. Let X~GIW(α1, θ, λ, β) and Y~GIW(α2, θ, λ, β). Then gX(y)/gY(y) = [α1^θ (1 − α1)(1 − α^{θ2}) / (α^{θ2} (1 − α2)(1 − α1^θ))] · [1 − (1 − α2)e^{−(λ/y)^β} / (1 − (1 − α1)e^{−(λ/y)^β})]^{θ+1}. Since α2 < α1, d/dx [gX(y)/gY(y)] = −(α1 − α2)(θ + 1) (λ/y)^β (β/y) e^{−(λ/y)^β} [1 − (1 − α2)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]^θ / [1 − (1 − α1)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]^{θ+2} < 0. Hence, gX(y)/gY(y) is decreasing in y. That is X ≤lr Y. The remaining statement follow from the implication (32).
